guides.title: Break into a building
guides.summary: Scout it, get inside, find what you came for, and get out before anyone notices.
guides.tip: Not every step needs a roll. If nothing is at stake (an empty building, no clock running), just say what happens and move on.

steps.t: Decide why you are going in
steps.x: Tie it to a vow or a case. Example: Night Owl is working the case "Who runs the Eastside docks?" and wants the shipping office's ledger. If the break-in is a big deal, give it its own small track (Troublesome or Dangerous). If it's one obstacle, a single roll or two is enough.

Watch from a rooftop across the street, roll +wits (observing) or +shadow (staying unseen). On a hit, take +2 momentum or +1 on your next move. Roll the Trouble Building oracle or City Location if you need to know what the building is. On a miss, your assumptions betray you: maybe there's a guard you didn't see. Pay the Price.

This is the risky part. Picking a lock quietly is +shadow. Climbing to a third-floor window is +edge. Prying a door is +iron. Kit helps: name the item you pull out ("lockpicks") and spend 1 Kit for +1, or +2 if the item is the whole answer. Strong hit: you're in clean, take +1 momentum. Weak hit: you're in, but make a suffer move (-1), like losing 1 momentum to a close call. Miss: Pay the Price. An alarm, a dog, or a camera that saw you (+1 Heat).

steps.t: Search for what you came for
steps.x: If this is for a case, use Work the Case +wits (examining records). Strong hit: add a clue and take +1 momentum. Weak hit: add a clue, but take +1 Heat, a suffer move, or advance a Nemesis scheme. Tap "Add clue" on the result, then turn the prompt into one concrete line on the case: "Personal and intimate, points toward family" might become "a child's drawing taped inside the safe." Not on a case? Use Gather Information instead.
A guard's flashlight, footsteps on the stairs. Hide with Face Danger +shadow. If it turns into a fight, use Enter the Fray +shadow (you're acting against an unaware foe) and see the fight guide.

steps.t: Get out and update the app
steps.x: Mark progress on your vow if you earned it (Reach a Milestone when you overcome a critical obstacle or gain meaningful insight). Clues you found are already on the case. Add Heat if anyone saw you or you broke into a public building. Write one line in the journal about what you found.

guides.title: A fight, step by step
guides.summary: Set an objective, track whether you are in control or in a bad spot, build progress, then finish it.
guides.tip: Two players: one of you can Aid Your Ally by Securing an Advantage or Gaining Ground for the other. For a fight that doesn't deserve the full treatment, use Battle: one roll and it's done.

steps.x: Decide what winning means: "take down the three dock thugs" or "grab the ledger and get out." Give it a rank (three armed thugs: Dangerous). On the Tracks tab, add a track of type combat with that rank.

Enter the Fray. Pick the stat by how the fight starts: on the move +edge, facing off +heart, close quarters +iron, ambushing an unaware foe +shadow, caught in a trap or sizing it up +wits. Strong hit: take +2 momentum and you are in control. Weak hit: choose one. Miss: you start in a bad spot.

When you're in control, Strike (+iron close, +edge at range). Strong hit: mark progress twice and stay in control. Weak hit: mark progress twice, but now you're in a bad spot. Or Gain Ground to set something up (a better position, cornering them): on a hit you stay in control and pick from mark progress, +2 momentum, or +1 on your next move.

steps.t: In a bad spot? Fight back or get out of the way
steps.x: When you're in a bad spot, Clash to trade blows: strong hit marks progress twice and puts you in control; weak hit marks progress once, but you stay in a bad spot and Pay the Price. Or React Under Fire to dodge, take cover or block: strong hit puts you back in control.

When Pay the Price means you get hurt, Endure Harm: -1 for a punch, -2 for a knife or a bad fall, -3 for a gunshot. Roll +health or +iron if your health hits 0 or you want to resist. Street versions of Toughness and Healing Factor help here.

When you have enough progress (four or five boxes is a fair shot), Take Decisive Action. This is a progress roll, but if you're in a bad spot, a strong hit counts as a weak hit and a weak hit counts as a miss. So get yourself in control first. Strong hit: you win. Weak hit: you win, at a cost. Miss: they win or the objective is lost.

Delete or close the combat track. If you beat a named foe, Reach a Milestone on any vow it serves. If a Boss or Villain escaped, or you won on a weak hit, add them as a Nemesis. Using lethal force? +1 Heat, and Code of Honor may have something to say about it.

guides.title: A night on patrol
guides.summary: Pick an area, find trouble, deal with it, and see how the neighborhood remembers you.
guides.tip: Rolling Trouble then City Location then Descriptor gives you a full scene in three taps.

steps.x: "Eastside docks, all night" in a rough area is Dangerous. Add a track of type patrol with that rank.

Pick your approach: rooftops +edge, staying hidden +shadow, talking to locals +heart, walking a visible beat +iron, police scanner +wits. Strong hit: mark progress and roll Trouble; you're there before it starts. Weak hit: mark progress and roll Trouble, but it's already happening and you choose a cost. Miss: no progress, Pay the Price. Any match: check scheme clocks, and if a Nemesis is locked up, run the escape check on the Tracks tab.

Play it out with normal moves. A mugging might be one Face Danger. A hostage situation might be a fight or a scene challenge. Kindness results are often just Compel or Aid moves, and they make good Heroics moments.
Strong hit with a match on Go On Patrol means Uncover a Plot: roll the Plot oracle, mark two ticks on Heroics, and decide whether to Open a Case.

Patrol two to four times in a night, then roll Finish Patrol on the track. Strong hit: Heroics reward by rank and lose 1 Heat. Weak hit: one rank lower. Miss: abandon it (Pay the Price, +1 Heat) or go back and fix it.

guides.title: Work a case from start to finish
guides.summary: No fixed answer: collect clues, build a theory together, and let the dice decide if it holds.
guides.tip: Weird clues are good. A theory that explains a smell of lilacs, a forged alibi and a missing dog in one story is the fun of this. Every clue it uses makes the roll better.

steps.x: Name it ("Who's poisoning the projects' water?") and set its complexity: Dangerous (1) is a good default, Formidable (2) for something big. Tie it to a vow, or Swear an Iron Vow. On the Tracks tab, add a track and set its type to case. Tap "+ Clue prompt" for a starting clue and "+ Suspect" once or twice.
Not you, not your partner, not the app. Don't decide who did it. Clues are just interesting facts. The truth is whatever theory you two prove later.

Each Work the Case is one lead: a crime scene (+wits), a witness (+heart), shaking down a fence (+iron), tailing someone (+shadow), racing to a scene (+edge). Strong hit: add a clue and +1 momentum. Weak hit: add a clue plus a cost. Miss: Pay the Price; on a match someone got there first, so cross off a clue.

steps.t: Turn the prompt into a clue
steps.x: A prompt like "A key, code or access card. Old, from years ago. Points toward: a hidden past." becomes one concrete line you write on the case: "a 1998 employee badge from the water treatment plant, in the victim's glovebox." Keep it specific, but don't explain it. Tap Twist when you want it messier.

steps.t: Let clues pick the next lead
steps.x: Each clue suggests somewhere to go. The badge means the next lead is the treatment plant, or someone who worked there in 1998. Investigator, Journalist and Enhanced Senses all help here.

When you have four or more clues, talk it through: who did it, why and how, using as many clues as you can. Tick each clue your theory explains. Stuck? "Ideas from the AI" offers three possible theories, but you two choose.

Your score is the clues used minus complexity. Five clues on a Dangerous case is a 4, seven clues is a 6. Strong hit: your theory is the truth, Reach a Milestone, +2 momentum, and the confrontation drops a rank. Weak hit: true, but they know you're coming, one detail is wrong, or you can't prove it yet. Miss: you're wrong; Pay the Price (+2 Heat if you accused someone) and find a new clue before trying again.
Now it's a fight, a chase, or a Compel. If they're a Boss or Villain who gets away, they become a Nemesis.

guides.title: Rescue from a burning building
guides.summary: Use a scene challenge: a progress track against a ticking tension clock.
guides.tip: The same setup works for a runaway train, a bomb, a collapsing parking garage, or a hostage standoff where the clock is the gunman's patience.

steps.x: Name the objective ("get the family out of the fourth floor"). Rank it: Troublesome if you have a clear advantage, Dangerous if you're ready, Formidable if you're outmatched. Add a track (type scene challenge) and a 4-segment clock named "Fire spreads."

Use the scene-challenge versions of Face Danger and Secure an Advantage. Kicking through a door +iron, finding the stairwell through smoke +wits, keeping a panicked kid calm +heart. Strong hit: mark progress (twice on a match). Weak hit: mark progress, but fill a clock segment. Miss: fill a segment (two on a match) and Pay the Price.
Smoke and fire mean Endure Harm. Someone you can't reach in time might mean Endure Stress.

When the clock fills or the track fills, or the story says it's over, roll Finish the Scene. Strong hit: everyone's out. Weak hit: success with a minor cost. Miss: a dire turn. A success marks Heroics (one tick for Dangerous, two for Formidable or higher).

guides.title: Interrogate a thug
guides.summary: Get a name out of someone who doesn't want to talk.

steps.x: Compel. Charm or make a deal +heart. Dangle them off a roof +iron. Bluff that their boss already sold them out +shadow. Strong hit: they talk, +1 momentum. Weak hit: they talk, but want something (protection, cash, to walk). Miss: they refuse or demand too much. Pay the Price.
Threats and violence draw attention. A miss on Compel is +1 Heat. Bloodthirsty or brutal methods add more. Vigilante helps if you hand them to a friendly cop instead.

If this is part of a case, make it a Work the Case +iron (shaking someone down) instead of a Compel, so a hit adds a clue to the case. Their answer is the clue: roll the prompt and make it what they let slip. Pick one move, not both.

guides.title: Between nights: recover and resupply
guides.summary: Patch up, clear your head, restock, and live your day life.
guides.tip: Your HQ lets you make recover moves there, but you can't Sojourn at it. Sojourn is for when you're out in the community.

steps.x: Heal. Getting stitched up by your Caretaker or a friendly ER nurse is +iron (treated by someone else). Mending yourself uses +iron or +wits, whichever is lower. Medbay and Caretaker add bonuses.
Hearten +heart: dinner with your family, a night at the bar with friends, time with someone who doesn't know about the mask. Caretaker and Independent help.
Resupply for shared Resources: work a shift (+heart), sell seized goods to a fence (+shadow), scavenge parts (+wits). Kit and Gadgeteer let you move Resources into Kit.
Skip patrolling for a session to lose 1 Heat. A press or police Connection covering for you also works.
Each filled box on a legacy track (Quests, Bonds, Heroics) earns 2 XP. Spend XP to take new assets or upgrade abilities (Advance). Track spent XP on your hero sheet.

guides.title: Playing with two heroes
guides.summary: Share the spotlight, help each other, and split up when the story wants it.

steps.x: One player describes and rolls, then the other. When you're together, whoever is closest to the danger usually goes.
Aid Your Ally: Secure an Advantage or Gain Ground on your partner's behalf, and they take the benefit. In a fight, a strong hit on Gain Ground puts you both in control.
Classic street-level move: one patrols, one works the case. Alternate scenes. Rolls and notes land in the shared journal, so nobody loses track.
A vow you both swear can be one shared track. Personal vows (your background vow) stay separate.

steps.t: Resources are shared, Heat is not
steps.x: Spending Resources drains you both. Heat is personal, so one reckless hero can be on the front page while the other stays a rumor.

guides.title: When a Nemesis moves
guides.summary: Scheme clocks, the plot going off, and the revolving door.

steps.x: On a match with Go On Patrol, Gather Information or Work the Case, advance one Nemesis's scheme clock. Also when a session ends and they went unopposed.
When the clock fills, roll All Hell Breaks Loose for how it hits the city, then Swear an Iron Vow (Extreme) to stop it or clean up after.
When you beat them, tap Lock up on the Tracks tab. Their scheme clears.
On a patrol match, run the escape check. On 1 to 3 on a d10, one locked-up Nemesis escapes, a rank tougher, with a new scheme. Generate villain on the Tracks tab rolls a fresh scheme if you need one.
